claims.claim_text: Condemnation of the massacre of dozens of men, women and children at mosques in Christchurch, New Zealand.
Support for survivors of the Christchurch mosque massacres.
Opposition to Islamophobia and readiness for DSA to defend religious minorities in its communities as part of anti-fascist organizing.
The principal Christchurch mosque attacker stated that racial hatred motivated him and that words from the U.S. far right and Donald Trump moved him to act.
The principal Christchurch mosque attacker was reportedly inspired by the white supremacist who murdered nine people at Charleston's Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church.
The principal Christchurch mosque attacker quoted the far-right terrorist who shot Norwegian Labour Party youth at a 2011 summer leadership training.
The principal Christchurch mosque attacker was undoubtedly aware of the Tree of Life Synagogue massacre in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
A rising international fascist movement threatens people of good conscience, undermines solidarity and spreads hatred and fear.
The international fascist movement seeks to divide the working class by race, religion and country and ultimately serve global elites' interests.
